text:
For pair production the centre‑of‑mass energy must satisfy  

\[
\sqrt{s}\ge 2m_ec^2 = 1.022\ \text{MeV}.
\]

For two photons of energies \(E_\gamma\) (high‑energy γ) and \(E_{\rm CMB}\) colliding head‑on (\(\theta=\pi\))  

\[
s = 2E_\gamma E_{\rm CMB}(1-\cos\theta)=4E_\gamma E_{\rm CMB}.
\]

Setting the threshold:

\[
4E_\gamma E_{\rm CMB}= (1.022\ \text{MeV})^{2}.
\]

With the average CMB photon energy \(E_{\rm CMB}=10^{-3}\,\text{eV}\),

\[
E_\gamma = \frac{(1.022\times10^{6}\,\text{eV})^{2}}{4\times10^{-3}\,\text{eV}}
          = \frac{1.045\times10^{12}\,\text{eV}^2}{4\times10^{-3}\,\text{eV}}
          \approx 2.6\times10^{14}\,\text{eV}
          = 2.6\times10^{5}\,\text{GeV}.
\]

Thus γ‑rays with energies of order \(2.6\times10^{5}\) GeV will be efficiently attenuated by pair production on the CMB.

**Answer: B**.
